sources.title: A comparison of reproductive strategies between island and mainland Caribbean Gesneriaceae
sources.design: 54 species studied under natural conditions: 28 insular Caribbean species and 26 mainland Costa Rica/Mexico species, with each species sampled at one study site
measured_links: autofertility index defined as bagged fruit set divided by outcross fruit set
sources.role: direct island-mainland functional-environment plus reproductive-dependency comparison

sources.title: Pollen limitation and reproductive assurance in Antillean Gesnerieae: a specialists vs. generalist comparison
sources.design: Antillean Gesnerieae with contrasting bat, hummingbird and generalist pollination systems; autonomous-selfing survey on 13 species and two-year pollen-supplementation experiments on nine species
measured_links: supplemental-pollen limitation of fruit and seed set

source_native_results.reproductive_assurance: autonomous selfing acted as reproductive assurance in three of four ornithophilous species
source_native_results.pollen_limitation: significant pollen limitation occurred in specialized bat- and hummingbird-pollinated species; none of four generalist species was pollen limited
source_native_results.exception: two ornithophilous Gesneria species with low hummingbird visitation and high autonomous self-pollination were not pollen limited

sources.title: Evolutionary breakdown of pollination specialization in a Caribbean plant radiation
sources.design: Antillean Gesnerieae phylogeny using nuclear markers plus morphology, with stochastic mapping of floral characters, pollination systems and breeding systems

source_native_results.bat_pollination_floral_response: associated with floral transitions matching the chiropterophilous syndrome

sources.role: evolutionary floral-response channel for the same Antillean radiation

cross_source_linkage.why_partial_not_complete: The programme has direct island-mainland visitation and autonomous-outcross dependency measurements, plus source-native pollen-limitation/reproductive-assurance experiments and independently reconstructed floral/pollination-system transitions in the same Antillean radiation. However, these are clade-level links assembled across studies rather than one matched population or tagged-plant panel, and no visit-level pollen deposition/effectiveness measure bridges visitor identity to pollen function.
cross_source_linkage.allowed_claim: This radiation independently supports a pathway in which low hummingbird visitation on islands co-occurs with reproductive-assurance and pollination-system alternatives, while floral transitions accompany repeated pollination-system evolution. It is a clade-level mechanistic recurrence, not a complete causal chain.
blocked_claims: do not infer per-visit pollinator effectiveness from visitation rate
do not treat pollination syndrome as effective dependency
do not treat the three source datasets as one matched population-level panel
do not infer that autonomous selfing is generally higher on islands because the 2015 island-mainland AFI comparison did not show that pattern
do not admit a formal cross-system mechanism effect until compatible estimands, uncertainty, provenance and independent system replication are available

comparison_with_nicotiana.complementary_strength: Nicotiana supplies direct per-visit/service information but crosses years for the dependency bridge; Caribbean Gesneriaceae supplies broad island-mainland dependency and evolutionary response replication but lacks visit-level pollen function.

next_actions: Recover stable source bytes or archival versions for the 2010 Ecology and New Phytologist studies and checksum them where lawful.
Extract species-level 2015 visitation and AFI rows with source locators and biological n, preserving phylogenetic non-independence.
Map which 2010 experimental species are represented in the 2015 island dataset before any cross-paper species-level linkage.
Search for source-native per-visit pollen deposition or single-visit reproductive-success data within the same Antillean Gesnerieae species.
Keep formal cross-system mechanism fitting closed until the missing effectiveness link and compatible independent-system estimands are resolved.
